description: We are Zero Dawn, and we're building Gaia: a multi-agent AI that watches over Earth's vital signs. One central agent commands specialist subagents that detect, analyze, and visualize how our planet is changing, using NASA's open Earth data. Like its namesake, Gaia exists to understand a changing world and tell its story. To potentially improve it!
summary:
GAIA (Geospatial Analysis & Investigation Assistant) helps people investigate changes in the Earth's systems using NASA data and reproducible analysis. Built for NASA Space Apps 2026’s “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge, GAIA turns an environmental question into a traceable investigation: she gathers supported observations, analyzes trends, coordinates relevant specialist functions, and presents sources, methods, uncertainty, and limitations alongside the findings.
GAIA matters because she helps people explore environmental trends and understand the impact we may or may not have on the earth and its ecosystem in hopes that they would try to heal the world together!
details:
GAIA is an ecological investigation workspace. Users can ask an environmental question, they may also define its place and time period, GAIA goes out, gathers data from NASA sources, reads literature, uses her subagents to crunch the numbers and do more research, then returns a detailed report of her findings. GAIA supports NASA MODIS satellite vegetation data and NASA POWER climate data, alongside registered analysis methods. Her specialist functions focus on atmosphere, water, plants, and animals; she can use the relevant functions rather than requiring every specialist for every question. Reports connect charts and findings to their data sources, methods, uncertainty, and known gaps.

For our worked example, GAIA analyzed Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) a measure of landscape greenness, not forest-only health across the selected BC Central Interior boundary from 2001 to 2024. The summer series showed a positive descriptive slope, but missing seasons prevented a confidence interval and p-value under the registered method. The monthly analysis was inconclusive because 187 of 288 months did not meet the coverage requirement. NASA POWER data showed summer warming at a nearby grid point; this is point-grid context, not a regional climate average or proof of what caused the greenness pattern.

GAIA’s intended impact is to make Earth-observation evidence more understandable and reproducible, while making it easier to see what the data can and cannot support in hopes that people would understand our impact on our planet, to educate them about what they do not know. Its creative contribution is combining conversational investigation, specialist perspectives, live data acquisition, and transparent statistical analysis in one workflow, with explicit safeguards against overclaiming causation.

The project uses JavaScript/Node.js, TypeScript/React, Rust/WebAssembly, and Python, including NumPy, SciPy, pandas, and statsmodels. It integrates NASA MODIS and NASA POWER data and preserves investigation inputs and provenance for numerical reproduction. We considered spatial and temporal coverage, data quality, missing observations, measurement support, uncertainty, and competing explanations.
